questions.prompt: Which pull requests should one run of the goal monitor?
questions.description: A single explicit target gives the loop a stable branch, review history, and terminal condition.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Require a repository and PR number or URL when launching the goal, and monitor only that PR during the run.

questions.prompt: What changes may the loop make without stopping for approval?
questions.description: The loop can remain useful and autonomous while still stopping before scope expansion or merge.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Allow warranted code/test/doc fixes on the PR branch, commits, pushes, review replies, and resolving fully addressed threads. Require approval for scope-expanding suggestions, destructive changes, force-pushes, base-branch changes, and any merge.

questions.prompt: What evidence should end the monitoring loop as ready to merge?
questions.description: The goal needs a quiescence rule so it does not declare victory before asynchronous reviewers finish checking the latest commit.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Require all required checks green, no actionable unresolved human or bot threads, every finding dispositioned with evidence, reviewers observed on the latest head commit, and two unchanged polls 5 minutes apart after the last completed review. Then report readiness and recommend merge method without merging.
